Subject: Pricing inquiry — prepay options for Foundry

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the cost transparency in Redwood Console. We're trying to build a simple procurement package for our seed-stage pricing model and want to explore prepay options. High level: 12–24 month prepay, want some flexibility on ramp (we expect usage to grow over the first 3–6 months), and would like a credits top-up to cover initial spikes.

Quick context: current monthly spend forecast is low ($3–6k) but we anticipate a jump to $20–35k/mo by month 6 if the pilot goes well. Procurement will need a simple billing cadence and a signed SOW. Can you send a sketch of a structure (tiered discount by term, ramped minimums, and how credits work)? Also please send any standard contract language around credit expiry and refunds.

Appreciate it — Eli

Eli — thanks for the clear context. Below is a quick sketch we use for early-stage prepay conversations; happy to run numbers if you share the month-by-month forecast (Karthik can take a look at expected token patterns).

Option A — 12 month prepay (flex)
- Term: 12 months, prepay paid up-front or in two equal invoices (Day 0, Day 180)
- Baseline discount vs retail: 12% off list for committed spend
- Ramped minimums: months 1–3 billed at 50% of committed monthly run rate (MRR); months 4–12 at 100% MRR
- Credits top-up: one-time onboarding credit equal to 15% of the committed dollar amount, applied to overage in months 1–3
- Credit expiry: credits valid for 12 months from invoice date; unused credits convert to service value (no cash refunds)

Option B — 24 month prepay (best value)
- Term: 24 months, annual billing in arrears allowed on credit-approved accounts, but prepay preferred for the higher discount
- Baseline discount: 20% off list for committed spend
- Ramped minimums: months 1–4 billed at 40% MRR, months 5–24 at 100% MRR
- Credits top-up: onboarding + scale credit (20% of year-1 committed amount), applied to overage or to offset initial over-provisioned capacity
- Early termination: pro-rated refund of unused prepaid month-value less an admin fee; legal to confirm

Other notes:
- Invoices: standard Net30; payments by ACH/credit card/wire
- Overage: consumed at retail list rates but offset by any remaining credits; we can cap month-to-month overage to avoid surprises
- SOW: we'll draft an SOW with the committed amounts and ramp schedule; revenue recognition will align to the SOW terms

If you want, Monica can prepare a side-by-side comparison and a simple numeric example with your forecast. Karthik, can you advise if these ramp percentages look reasonable from an infra/billing perspective?

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Growth, Redwood Inference

For numbers: attached is a conservative month-by-month projection for the first 12 months (expected ramp to $28k/mo by month 6). If you can produce a simple table showing committed amount, effective discount, and monthly billed minimums for both 12m and 24m options, that would speed approval.

Eli — appreciate the forecast; we ran the numbers and here's a concrete proposal that maps to your procurement asks. Attaching a one-page commercial summary and a redlineable SOW.

Commercial summary (high level):
- 12-month Flex Prepay
  - Committed annual value: $180,000 (equivalent to $15k/mo committed)
  - Prepay invoicing: two installments: $90k at signing, $90k at month 6
  - Effective discount vs retail: ~12%
  - Ramp billing: months 1–3 billed at 50% of $15k = $7,500; months 4–12 billed at 100% = $15k
  - Onboarding credit: $27,000 (15% of committed), valid 12 months; applied to overage or partner integration line items per SOW

- 24-month Value Prepay
  - Committed first-year value: $300,000 (equivalent to $25k/mo committed year 1), total committed = $600k over 24 months
  - Prepay invoicing: annual in advance (preferred) or annual in arrears by mutual agreement
  - Effective discount vs retail: ~20% (applies to committed units)
  - Ramp billing: months 1–4 billed at 40% of $25k = $10k; months 5–24 billed at 100% = $25k
  - Onboarding + scale credit: $60,000 (20% of year-1 committed), valid 12 months; credits can be applied to integrations or Redwood billed services (no cash-outs)
  - Annual billing: we can issue year-1 invoice at signing and year-2 invoice 12 months later; if you'd prefer both years invoiced at signing, we can discuss an incremental 2% additional discount to compensate cashflow impact

Refund / credit policy (procurement asks):
- Credits expire 12 months from their issuance date. Unused credits are converted to account service value; Redwood does not issue cash refunds for applied credits except where a termination clause triggers a pro-rated refund on unused prepaid amounts (less an administrative fee).
- If committed MRR materially exceeds usage for a sustained period (90 days), procurement can request a one-time commitment reduction to be negotiated; reductions require 60–90 days notice and may be accompanied by re-pricing for future months.
- Early termination: pro-rata refund of unused prepaid service value for months remaining in the prepaid period, less a 3% admin fee and any consumed onboarding credits. Legal to confirm final language in SOW/SLA.

Operational items / next steps:
1) Monica will prepare a side-by-side Excel showing the numbers per your attached forecast (see attached foundry_usage_forecast.xlsx with applied math).
2) I'll have Legal produce a SOW draft and the related billing schedule — will send a DocuSign link for signature once commercial is agreed.
3) Karthik will scope recommended token limits and guardrails to avoid unexpected overage during initial ramp; we can add a monthly overage cap for the first 6 months if you want.

If this looks broadly aligned, please confirm which option you prefer (12m Flex or 24m Value) and whether Foundry's finance team wants annual billing on the 24m option. Once you confirm, we'll send a clean SOW and a DocuSign.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
